nodes.name: Red oat grass
nodes.desc: A tall tussock grass of African grasslands and a recorded food of wildebeest, zebra, buffalo and gazelles in the GloBI database.

nodes.name: Bermuda grass
nodes.desc: A low, spreading grass that carpets grazed ground and is recorded as food for many of the crater grazers.

nodes.name: Umbrella thorn
nodes.desc: A flat-topped thorny tree. Its leaves and pods are browsed by elephants and black rhinos, which prefer acacias.

nodes.name: Spirulina algae
nodes.desc: A blue-green alga that thrives in very alkaline water and is the main food of lesser flamingos on East African soda lakes.

nodes.name: Blue wildebeest
nodes.desc: The most numerous large grazer on the crater floor, though counts have fallen from about 14,700 in 1986 to about 7,250 in the mid-2000s. The most common medium-sized prey of hyenas here.

nodes.name: Plains zebra
nodes.desc: Grazes alongside wildebeest on the crater floor and in the surrounding plains, and is a regular prey of lions and hyenas.

nodes.name: African buffalo
nodes.desc: Numbers have grown in the crater, possibly because fire suppression has favoured tall, fibrous grass. Hyenas largely avoid them, but lions hunt them.

nodes.name: Thomson's gazelle
nodes.desc: A small grazer of the short-grass plains and crater floor that is hunted by lions, hyenas and jackals.

nodes.name: Black rhinoceros
nodes.desc: A browser of leafy plants, twigs and thorny shoots that favours acacias. The crater population fell to 13 in 1993 and had recovered to 55 by 2018.

nodes.name: African elephant
nodes.desc: A huge mixed feeder that eats grass as well as browsing acacia and other trees, opening up woodland.

nodes.name: Lesser flamingo
nodes.desc: Filters spirulina from alkaline water with its specialised bill. Thousands gather at shallow Lake Magadi on the crater floor, where hyenas prey on them.

nodes.name: Brush-furred mice
nodes.desc: Small rodents of the highland grass and scrub, a staple prey for servals and jackals.

nodes.name: African golden wolf
nodes.desc: A small canid that hunts rodents and young antelope and scavenges leftovers from larger carnivores.

nodes.name: Serval
nodes.desc: A long-legged cat that is widespread in the crater and pounces on rodents in tall grass.

nodes.name: White-backed vulture
nodes.desc: Soars over the plains and feeds on the carcasses of wildebeest, zebra, buffalo and other animals that die or are killed.

nodes.name: Lion
nodes.desc: The crater holds one of the densest lion populations known, about 62 animals in 2001, but it is inbred and has suffered disease die-offs.

nodes.name: Spotted hyena
nodes.desc: A top predator in the crater. Studies in Ngorongoro found it hunts as much as lions, and lions often take over its kills.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Equatorial sun drives growth of grass, trees and the algae in the shallow lake.

nodes.name: Seasonal rains
nodes.desc: Rains fall in a wet season from about December and draw the large migratory herds on the plains around the crater.

nodes.name: Lake Magadi
nodes.desc: A shallow, seasonal soda lake in the south-west of the crater, fed mainly by the Munge Stream. Its alkaline water grows the algae flamingos eat.

nodes.name: Volcanic soil
nodes.desc: Fertile soils of the old volcano feed the crater grassland.

nodes.name: Dung beetles, fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
